ko.title: 2,983개의 이름, 일곱 번의 묵념: 9/11 메모리얼 25주년 추모식 현장

segments.src: Twenty-five years to the day, the plaza at the National September 11 Memorial in Lower Manhattan filled once again with families holding photographs, folded flags, and small handwritten notes.
segments.tr: 정확히 25년이 지난 오늘, 로어맨해튼의 국립 9/11 메모리얼 광장은 사진과 접힌 국기, 손으로 쓴 작은 쪽지를 든 유가족들로 다시 한번 가득 찼습니다.

segments.src: One by one, relatives stepped up to the microphones to read aloud the names of the 2,983 people killed in the attacks of September 11, 2001, and in the 1993 bombing of the World Trade Center.
segments.tr: 유가족들은 차례로 마이크 앞으로 나아가 2001년 9월 11일 테러와 1993년 세계무역센터 폭탄 테러로 희생된 2,983명의 이름을 한 사람씩 큰 소리로 낭독했습니다.

segments.src: The reading, a tradition that has anchored the anniversary since the first year after the attacks, stretched across the morning as it has every year — but this quarter-century mark carried a weight of its own.
segments.tr: 테러 발생 첫해부터 매년 추모식의 중심을 잡아온 전통인 이름 낭독은 예년과 마찬가지로 오전 내내 이어졌지만, 이번 25주년이라는 이정표는 그 자체로 남다른 무게감을 더했습니다.

segments.src: ## A Morning of Seven Silences
segments.tr: ## 일곱 번의 묵념이 흐른 아침

segments.src: The ceremony was structured, as always, around moments of silence that correspond to the timeline of that morning: the moment American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower, the moment United Airlines Flight 175 struck the South Tower, the moment American Airlines Flight 77 struck the Pentagon, the moment Flight 93 went down in a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, and the moments each tower fell.
segments.tr: 추모식은 언제나처럼 그날 아침의 시간대에 맞춘 묵념의 순간들을 중심으로 진행되었습니다. 아메리칸 항공 11편이 북쪽 타워에 충돌한 순간, 유나이티드 항공 175편이 남쪽 타워에 충돌한 순간, 아메리칸 항공 77편이 펜타곤에 충돌한 순간, 93편이 펜실베이니아주 섕크스빌 인근 들판에 추락한 순간, 그리고 각 타워가 붕괴한 순간들이 그것입니다.

segments.src: Seven pauses in total, observed in near-total silence by the crowd gathered around the memorial's twin reflecting pools.
segments.tr: 메모리얼의 쌍둥이 반사 풀 주변에 모인 군중이 거의 완벽한 침묵 속에서 지킨 묵념은 총 일곱 번이었습니다.

segments.src: Bells tolled at the start of each pause.
segments.tr: 매 묵념이 시작될 때마다 종소리가 울려 퍼졌습니다.

segments.src: Many in attendance placed a hand over their heart; others simply stood still, eyes on the bronze parapets where the names of the dead are inscribed.
segments.tr: 참석자 중 상당수는 가슴에 손을 얹었고, 다른 이들은 희생자들의 이름이 새겨진 청동 난간에 시선을 고정한 채 그저 묵묵히 서 있었습니다.

segments.src: For families who have attended every anniversary since 2002, the rhythm of the ceremony is familiar.
segments.tr: 2002년부터 매년 추모식에 참석해 온 유가족들에게 이 의식의 리듬은 익숙합니다.

segments.src: For a younger generation attending for the first time — some too young to have been alive in 2001 — organizers say the ceremony has increasingly become a moment of historical connection as much as personal grief.
segments.tr: 처음으로 참석하는 젊은 세대(일부는 2001년 당시 태어나지도 않았을 만큼 어린 세대)에게 이 추모식은 개인적인 슬픔뿐만 아니라 역사적 연결의 순간이 되어가고 있다고 주최 측은 전합니다.

segments.src: ## Names Read by the Next Generation
segments.tr: ## 다음 세대가 낭독하는 이름들

segments.src: A notable feature of this year's reading was the number of children and grandchildren of victims taking the microphone, some reading a parent's or grandparent's name for the first time.
segments.tr: 올해 이름 낭독에서 눈에 띄는 특징은 희생자의 자녀와 손자녀들이 마이크를 잡은 경우가 많았다는 점이며, 일부는 부모나 조부모의 이름을 처음으로 낭독하기도 했습니다.

segments.src: Memorial organizers noted that as the population of surviving spouses and siblings ages, the responsibility of remembrance is passing to younger relatives — a shift that has shaped the tone of the ceremony in recent years toward continuity and legacy rather than only mourning.
segments.tr: 메모리얼 주최 측은 생존한 배우자와 형제자매들이 고령화됨에 따라 추모의 책임이 더 젊은 친족들에게 넘어가고 있다고 언급했습니다. 이러한 변화는 최근 몇 년 동안 추모식의 분위기를 단순한 애도를 넘어 지속성과 유산의 전수로 형성하는 데 기여했습니다.

segments.src: Family members were also permitted, as in past years, to add brief personal remarks after reading each name — a line about a loved one's laugh, their profession, or a milestone the family has marked without them.
segments.tr: 유가족들은 예년과 마찬가지로 각 이름을 낭독한 후 짧은 개인적 소회를 덧붙일 수 있었습니다. 사랑하는 이의 웃음소리, 그들의 직업, 혹은 그들 없이 가족이 맞이한 기념비적인 순간들에 대한 한 줄의 이야기였습니다.

segments.src: Memorial staff say these additions, while brief, have become one of the most meaningful parts of the day for attendees.
segments.tr: 메모리얼 스태프들은 비록 짧지만 이러한 덧붙임이 참석자들에게 하루 중 가장 뜻깊은 부분 중 하나가 되었다고 말합니다.

segments.src: ## Tributes Beyond Manhattan
segments.tr: ## 맨해튼을 넘어선 추모의 물결

segments.src: The commemorations extended well beyond the World Trade Center plaza.
segments.tr: 추모 행사는 세계무역센터 광장을 넘어 널리 퍼져나갔습니다.

segments.src: At the Pentagon Memorial in Arlington, Virginia, a separate ceremony honored the 184 people killed there, including those aboard Flight 77.
segments.tr: 버지니아주 알링턴의 펜타곤 메모리얼에서는 77편 탑승자들을 포함해 그곳에서 목숨을 잃은 184명을 기리는 별도의 추모식이 열렸습니다.

segments.src: In Shanksville, Pennsylvania, the Flight 93 National Memorial held its own observance for the 40 passengers and crew who died after confronting hijackers, an act widely credited with preventing further attacks in Washington, D.C.
segments.tr: 펜실베이니아주 섕크스빌의 93편 국립 메모리얼에서는 납치범들에게 맞서 싸우다 사망한 40명의 승객과 승무원을 위한 자체 추모식이 열렸습니다. 이들의 행동은 워싱턴 D.C.를 겨냥한 추가 테러를 막아낸 것으로 널리 인정받고 있습니다.

segments.src: Across New York City, firehouses, police precincts, and civic buildings held their own smaller tributes throughout the day, honoring the first responders — including the 343 firefighters and dozens of police officers — who died in the rescue efforts.
segments.tr: 뉴욕시 전역의 소방서, 경찰서, 관공서 건물에서도 하루 종일 자체적인 소규모 추모 행사가 열려, 구조 작업 중 사망한 343명의 소방관과 수십 명의 경찰관을 포함한 첫 대응자들을 기렸습니다.

segments.src: Flags were lowered to half-staff at federal buildings nationwide, and moments of local remembrance were reported in communities across the country, reflecting how the events of that day touched nearly every state.
segments.tr: 전국의 연방 건물에는 조기가 게양되었으며, 전국 각지 공동체에서 지역별 추모의 순간들이 보고되어 그날의 사건이 거의 모든 주에 어떻게 닿았는지를 보여주었습니다.

segments.src: ## A Quarter-Century of Remembrance
segments.tr: ## 4분의 1세기 동안 이어진 추모

segments.src: Twenty-five years on, officials at the memorial say the annual reading remains one of the largest sustained acts of collective remembrance in the country.
segments.tr: 25년이 지난 지금, 메모리얼 관계자들은 매년 열리는 이름 낭독이 미국에서 가장 오랫동안 지속되어 온 집단적 추모 행위 중 하나로 남아있다고 말합니다.

segments.src: The names are read not in isolation but grouped where possible with family members' requests — husbands near wives, colleagues near colleagues — a practice memorial staff describe as an effort to preserve human connections in the record of the day.
segments.tr: 이름들은 무작위로 낭독되는 것이 아니라, 가능한 한 유가족의 요청에 따라 남편은 아내 곁에, 동료는 동료 곁에 배치되어 낭독됩니다. 메모리얼 스태프들은 이를 그날의 기록 속에서 인간적인 유대를 보존하려는 노력이라고 설명합니다.

segments.src: As the ceremony closed, attendees were invited to make paper rubbings of names etched into the memorial's bronze panels, a quiet ritual that has become part of the memorial's daily life beyond the anniversary itself.
segments.tr: 추모식이 끝나갈 무렵, 참석자들은 메모리얼의 청동 패널에 새겨진 이름을 종이에 대고 문지르는 탁본 체험에 초대받았습니다. 이 조용한 의식은 추모일 자체를 넘어 메모리얼의 일상적인 풍경이 되었습니다.

segments.src: For many families, the 25th anniversary was less about a milestone number than about ensuring the names — and the people behind them — continue to be spoken aloud, year after year.
segments.tr: 많은 유가족에게 이번 25주년은 25라는 숫자 자체보다는, 그 이름들과 그 뒤에 있는 사람들이 해마다 계속해서 세상에 불려지도록 보장하는 일에 더 큰 의미가 있었습니다.

zh.title: 2,983个名字，七次静默：走进“9·11”纪念馆25周年纪念仪式

segments.src: Twenty-five years to the day, the plaza at the National September 11 Memorial in Lower Manhattan filled once again with families holding photographs, folded flags, and small handwritten notes.
segments.tr: 二十五年后的这一天，位于曼哈顿下城的“9·11”国家纪念广场再次挤满了手持照片、折叠旗帜和手写小纸条的家属。

segments.src: One by one, relatives stepped up to the microphones to read aloud the names of the 2,983 people killed in the attacks of September 11, 2001, and in the 1993 bombing of the World Trade Center.
segments.tr: 亲属们一个接一个地走上麦克风，大声读出在2001年9月11日的袭击事件以及1993年世界贸易中心爆炸案中遇难的2,983人的名字。

segments.src: The reading, a tradition that has anchored the anniversary since the first year after the attacks, stretched across the morning as it has every year — but this quarter-century mark carried a weight of its own.
segments.tr: 这场朗读仪式自袭击发生后的第一年起就成为了纪念日的支柱，像往年一样贯穿了整个上午——但这个四分之一个世纪的节点有着特殊的意义。

segments.src: ## A Morning of Seven Silences
segments.tr: ## 七次静默的早晨

segments.src: The ceremony was structured, as always, around moments of silence that correspond to the timeline of that morning: the moment American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower, the moment United Airlines Flight 175 struck the South Tower, the moment American Airlines Flight 77 struck the Pentagon, the moment Flight 93 went down in a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, and the moments each tower fell.
segments.tr: 仪式一如既往地围绕着与那天早晨时间线相对应的默哀时刻进行：美国航空11号航班撞击北塔的时刻、联合航空175号航班撞击南塔的时刻、美国航空77号航班撞击五角大楼的时刻、93号航班在宾夕法尼亚州尚克斯维尔附近坠毁的时刻，以及两座塔楼倒塌的时刻。

segments.src: Seven pauses in total, observed in near-total silence by the crowd gathered around the memorial's twin reflecting pools.
segments.tr: 总共七次暂停，聚集在纪念馆双倒影池周围的人群在近乎绝对的寂静中进行默哀。

segments.src: Bells tolled at the start of each pause.
segments.tr: 每次暂停开始时，钟声都会响起。

segments.src: Many in attendance placed a hand over their heart; others simply stood still, eyes on the bronze parapets where the names of the dead are inscribed.
segments.tr: 许多出席者将手放在胸前；其他人则静静地站着，目光注视着刻有逝者名字的青铜护栏。

segments.src: For families who have attended every anniversary since 2002, the rhythm of the ceremony is familiar.
segments.tr: 对于自2002年以来每年都参加纪念活动的家庭来说，仪式的节奏早已熟悉。

segments.src: For a younger generation attending for the first time — some too young to have been alive in 2001 — organizers say the ceremony has increasingly become a moment of historical connection as much as personal grief.
segments.tr: 对于第一次参加的年轻一代——其中一些人在2001年时甚至尚未出生——组织者表示，这场仪式已日益成为一种历史连接，其意义不亚于个人悲伤。

segments.src: ## Names Read by the Next Generation
segments.tr: ## 下一代朗读名字

segments.src: A notable feature of this year's reading was the number of children and grandchildren of victims taking the microphone, some reading a parent's or grandparent's name for the first time.
segments.tr: 今年朗读仪式的一个显著特点是，许多遇难者的子女和孙辈走上麦克风，有些人是第一次读出父母或祖父母的名字。

segments.src: Memorial organizers noted that as the population of surviving spouses and siblings ages, the responsibility of remembrance is passing to younger relatives — a shift that has shaped the tone of the ceremony in recent years toward continuity and legacy rather than only mourning.
segments.tr: 纪念馆组织者指出，随着幸存配偶和兄弟姐妹年龄的增长，纪念的责任正在传递给年轻的亲属——这一转变使得近年来仪式的基调更多地转向了延续和传承，而不仅仅是哀悼。

segments.src: Family members were also permitted, as in past years, to add brief personal remarks after reading each name — a line about a loved one's laugh, their profession, or a milestone the family has marked without them.
segments.tr: 与往年一样，家属们在读完每个名字后，也被允许添加简短的个人感言——比如关于亲人的笑声、他们的职业，或是家庭在没有他们的情况下所经历的重要里程碑。

segments.src: Memorial staff say these additions, while brief, have become one of the most meaningful parts of the day for attendees.
segments.tr: 纪念馆工作人员表示，这些补充内容虽然简短，却已成为出席者当天最有意义的部分之一。

segments.src: ## Tributes Beyond Manhattan
segments.tr: ## 曼哈顿之外的致敬

segments.src: The commemorations extended well beyond the World Trade Center plaza.
segments.tr: 纪念活动远远超出了世界贸易中心广场的范围。

segments.src: At the Pentagon Memorial in Arlington, Virginia, a separate ceremony honored the 184 people killed there, including those aboard Flight 77.
segments.tr: 在弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿的五角大楼纪念馆，一场单独的仪式纪念了在那里遇难的184人，其中包括77号航班上的乘客。

segments.src: In Shanksville, Pennsylvania, the Flight 93 National Memorial held its own observance for the 40 passengers and crew who died after confronting hijackers, an act widely credited with preventing further attacks in Washington, D.C.
segments.tr: 在宾夕法尼亚州尚克斯维尔，93号航班国家纪念馆为40名在反抗劫机者后牺牲的乘客和机组人员举行了纪念活动，这一英勇行为被广泛认为是阻止了针对华盛顿特区的进一步袭击。

segments.src: Across New York City, firehouses, police precincts, and civic buildings held their own smaller tributes throughout the day, honoring the first responders — including the 343 firefighters and dozens of police officers — who died in the rescue efforts.
segments.tr: 在整个纽约市，消防站、警察分局和市政建筑全天都举行了各自的小型致敬活动，纪念在救援行动中牺牲的急救人员——包括343名消防员和数十名警察。

segments.src: Flags were lowered to half-staff at federal buildings nationwide, and moments of local remembrance were reported in communities across the country, reflecting how the events of that day touched nearly every state.
segments.tr: 全国各地的联邦大楼降半旗致哀，全国各地的社区也报告了当地的纪念时刻，反映出那一天的事件触及了几乎每一个州。

segments.src: ## A Quarter-Century of Remembrance
segments.tr: ## 四分之一个世纪的缅怀

segments.src: Twenty-five years on, officials at the memorial say the annual reading remains one of the largest sustained acts of collective remembrance in the country.
segments.tr: 二十五年过去了，纪念馆的官员表示，年度朗读活动仍然是全国规模最大的持续性集体纪念活动之一。

segments.src: The names are read not in isolation but grouped where possible with family members' requests — husbands near wives, colleagues near colleagues — a practice memorial staff describe as an effort to preserve human connections in the record of the day.
segments.tr: 名字的朗读并非孤立进行，而是尽可能根据家属的要求进行分组——丈夫与妻子在一起，同事与同事在一起——纪念馆工作人员将这种做法描述为在当天的记录中努力保存人际联系。

segments.src: As the ceremony closed, attendees were invited to make paper rubbings of names etched into the memorial's bronze panels, a quiet ritual that has become part of the memorial's daily life beyond the anniversary itself.
segments.tr: 仪式结束时，出席者被邀请对刻在纪念馆青铜板上的名字进行纸上拓印，这是一种安静的仪式，已成为纪念馆日常生活中超越纪念日本身的一部分。

segments.src: For many families, the 25th anniversary was less about a milestone number than about ensuring the names — and the people behind them — continue to be spoken aloud, year after year.
segments.tr: 对于许多家庭来说，25周年纪念与其说是一个里程碑式的数字，不如说是为了确保这些名字——以及名字背后的人——能够年复一年地被大声读出。

segments.tr: एक-एक करके, रिश्तेदार माइक्रोफोन के पास आए और 11 सितंबर, 2001 के हमलों और 1993 में वर्ल्ड ट्रेड सेंटर में हुए बम विस्फोट में मारे गए 2,983 लोगों के नाम जोर-जोर से पढ़े।

segments.src: The reading, a tradition that has anchored the anniversary since the first year after the attacks, stretched across the morning as it has every year — but this quarter-century mark carried a weight of its own.
segments.tr: यह पाठ, एक ऐसी परंपरा जिसने हमलों के बाद पहले साल से ही वर्षगांठ को आधार प्रदान किया है, हर साल की तरह पूरी सुबह चलता रहा — लेकिन इस पच्चीस साल के पड़ाव का अपना ही एक महत्व था।

segments.src: ## A Morning of Seven Silences
segments.tr: ## सात मौन की एक सुबह

segments.src: The ceremony was structured, as always, around moments of silence that correspond to the timeline of that morning: the moment American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower, the moment United Airlines Flight 175 struck the South Tower, the moment American Airlines Flight 77 struck the Pentagon, the moment Flight 93 went down in a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, and the moments each tower fell.
segments.tr: समारोह हमेशा की तरह उस सुबह की समयरेखा के अनुरूप मौन के क्षणों के इर्द-गिर्द आयोजित किया गया था: वह क्षण जब अमेरिकन एयरलाइंस की उड़ान 11 नॉर्थ टॉवर से टकराई, वह क्षण जब यूनाइटेड एयरलाइंस की उड़ान 175 साउथ टॉवर से टकराई, वह क्षण जब अमेरिकन एयरलाइंस की उड़ान 77 पेंटागन से टकराई, वह क्षण जब उड़ान 93 शैंक्सविले, पेंसिल्वेनिया के पास एक खेत में दुर्घटनाग्रस्त हुई, और वे क्षण जब प्रत्येक टॉवर गिरा।

segments.src: Seven pauses in total, observed in near-total silence by the crowd gathered around the memorial's twin reflecting pools.
segments.tr: कुल सात ठहराव, जिन्हें मेमोरियल के जुड़वां रिफ्लेक्टिंग पूल के चारों ओर जमा भीड़ द्वारा लगभग पूर्ण मौन में मनाया गया।

segments.src: Bells tolled at the start of each pause.
segments.tr: प्रत्येक ठहराव की शुरुआत में घंटियां बजाई गईं।

segments.src: Many in attendance placed a hand over their heart; others simply stood still, eyes on the bronze parapets where the names of the dead are inscribed.
segments.tr: उपस्थित कई लोगों ने अपने दिल पर हाथ रखा; अन्य बस स्थिर खड़े रहे, उनकी नजरें उन कांस्य पैरापेट्स पर थीं जहाँ मृतकों के नाम अंकित हैं।

segments.src: For families who have attended every anniversary since 2002, the rhythm of the ceremony is familiar.
segments.tr: 2002 से हर वर्षगांठ में शामिल होने वाले परिवारों के लिए, समारोह की लय परिचित है।

segments.src: For a younger generation attending for the first time — some too young to have been alive in 2001 — organizers say the ceremony has increasingly become a moment of historical connection as much as personal grief.
segments.tr: पहली बार भाग लेने वाली युवा पीढ़ी के लिए — जिनमें से कुछ 2001 में पैदा भी नहीं हुए थे — आयोजकों का कहना है कि यह समारोह व्यक्तिगत शोक के साथ-साथ ऐतिहासिक जुड़ाव का क्षण भी बनता जा रहा है।

segments.src: ## Names Read by the Next Generation
segments.tr: ## अगली पीढ़ी द्वारा पढ़े गए नाम

segments.src: A notable feature of this year's reading was the number of children and grandchildren of victims taking the microphone, some reading a parent's or grandparent's name for the first time.
segments.tr: इस वर्ष के पाठ की एक उल्लेखनीय विशेषता पीड़ितों के बच्चों और पोते-पोतियों की बड़ी संख्या थी जो माइक्रोफोन के पास आए, जिनमें से कुछ ने पहली बार अपने माता-पिता या दादा-दादी का नाम पढ़ा।

segments.src: Memorial organizers noted that as the population of surviving spouses and siblings ages, the responsibility of remembrance is passing to younger relatives — a shift that has shaped the tone of the ceremony in recent years toward continuity and legacy rather than only mourning.
segments.tr: मेमोरियल के आयोजकों ने उल्लेख किया कि जैसे-जैसे जीवित जीवनसाथी और भाई-बहनों की आबादी उम्रदराज हो रही है, स्मरण की जिम्मेदारी युवा रिश्तेदारों को सौंपी जा रही है — एक ऐसा बदलाव जिसने हाल के वर्षों में समारोह के लहजे को केवल शोक के बजाय निरंतरता और विरासत की ओर मोड़ दिया है।

segments.src: Family members were also permitted, as in past years, to add brief personal remarks after reading each name — a line about a loved one's laugh, their profession, or a milestone the family has marked without them.
segments.tr: पिछले वर्षों की तरह, परिवार के सदस्यों को प्रत्येक नाम पढ़ने के बाद संक्षिप्त व्यक्तिगत टिप्पणी जोड़ने की भी अनुमति दी गई थी — किसी प्रियजन की हंसी, उनके पेशे, या परिवार द्वारा उनके बिना मनाए गए किसी मील के पत्थर के बारे में एक पंक्ति।

segments.src: Memorial staff say these additions, while brief, have become one of the most meaningful parts of the day for attendees.
segments.tr: मेमोरियल के कर्मचारियों का कहना है कि ये टिप्पणियां, हालांकि संक्षिप्त हैं, उपस्थित लोगों के लिए दिन के सबसे सार्थक हिस्सों में से एक बन गई हैं।

segments.src: ## Tributes Beyond Manhattan
segments.tr: ## मैनहट्टन से परे श्रद्धांजलि

segments.src: The commemorations extended well beyond the World Trade Center plaza.
segments.tr: स्मरणोत्सव वर्ल्ड ट्रेड सेंटर प्लाजा से कहीं आगे तक फैल गए।

segments.src: At the Pentagon Memorial in Arlington, Virginia, a separate ceremony honored the 184 people killed there, including those aboard Flight 77.
segments.tr: आर्लिंगटन, वर्जीनिया में पेंटागन मेमोरियल में, एक अलग समारोह में वहां मारे गए 184 लोगों को सम्मानित किया गया, जिसमें उड़ान 77 में सवार लोग भी शामिल थे।

segments.src: In Shanksville, Pennsylvania, the Flight 93 National Memorial held its own observance for the 40 passengers and crew who died after confronting hijackers, an act widely credited with preventing further attacks in Washington, D.C.
segments.tr: शैंक्सविले, पेंसिल्वेनिया में, फ्लाइट 93 नेशनल मेमोरियल ने उन 40 यात्रियों और चालक दल के सदस्यों के लिए अपना स्वयं का स्मरणोत्सव आयोजित किया, जो अपहरणकर्ताओं का सामना करने के बाद मारे गए थे, एक ऐसा कार्य जिसे व्यापक रूप से वाशिंगटन, डी.सी. में और अधिक हमलों को रोकने का श्रेय दिया जाता है।

segments.src: Across New York City, firehouses, police precincts, and civic buildings held their own smaller tributes throughout the day, honoring the first responders — including the 343 firefighters and dozens of police officers — who died in the rescue efforts.
segments.tr: पूरे न्यूयॉर्क शहर में, फायरहाउस, पुलिस थानों और नागरिक भवनों ने दिन भर अपनी छोटी-छोटी श्रद्धांजलि सभाएं आयोजित कीं, जिसमें उन प्रथम उत्तरदाताओं को सम्मानित किया गया — जिनमें 343 अग्निशामक और दर्जनों पुलिस अधिकारी शामिल थे — जो बचाव कार्यों में मारे गए थे।

segments.src: Flags were lowered to half-staff at federal buildings nationwide, and moments of local remembrance were reported in communities across the country, reflecting how the events of that day touched nearly every state.
segments.tr: देश भर के संघीय भवनों में झंडे आधे झुका दिए गए थे, और देश भर के समुदायों में स्थानीय स्मरण के क्षणों की सूचना मिली, जो यह दर्शाता है कि उस दिन की घटनाओं ने लगभग हर राज्य को कैसे प्रभावित किया।

segments.src: ## A Quarter-Century of Remembrance
segments.tr: ## स्मरण की एक चौथाई सदी

segments.src: Twenty-five years on, officials at the memorial say the annual reading remains one of the largest sustained acts of collective remembrance in the country.
segments.tr: पच्चीस साल बाद, मेमोरियल के अधिकारियों का कहना है कि वार्षिक पाठ देश में सामूहिक स्मरण के सबसे बड़े निरंतर कार्यों में से एक बना हुआ है।

segments.src: The names are read not in isolation but grouped where possible with family members' requests — husbands near wives, colleagues near colleagues — a practice memorial staff describe as an effort to preserve human connections in the record of the day.
segments.tr: नामों को अलग-थलग नहीं बल्कि जहां संभव हो परिवार के सदस्यों के अनुरोधों के साथ समूहीकृत करके पढ़ा जाता है — पत्नियों के पास पति, सहकर्मियों के पास सहकर्मी — एक ऐसी प्रथा जिसे मेमोरियल के कर्मचारी दिन के रिकॉर्ड में मानवीय संबंधों को संरक्षित करने के प्रयास के रूप में वर्णित करते हैं।

segments.src: As the ceremony closed, attendees were invited to make paper rubbings of names etched into the memorial's bronze panels, a quiet ritual that has become part of the memorial's daily life beyond the anniversary itself.
segments.tr: जैसे ही समारोह समाप्त हुआ, उपस्थित लोगों को मेमोरियल के कांस्य पैनलों पर उकेरे गए नामों की पेपर रूबिंग (छाप) लेने के लिए आमंत्रित किया गया, एक शांत अनुष्ठान जो वर्षगांठ से परे मेमोरियल के दैनिक जीवन का हिस्सा बन गया है।

segments.src: For many families, the 25th anniversary was less about a milestone number than about ensuring the names — and the people behind them — continue to be spoken aloud, year after year.
segments.tr: कई परिवारों के लिए, 25वीं वर्षगांठ एक मील के पत्थर की संख्या के बारे में कम थी, और इस बारे में अधिक थी कि नामों — और उनके पीछे के लोगों — को साल-दर-साल जोर-जोर से बोला जाना सुनिश्चित किया जाए।

es.title: 2.983 nombres, siete silencios: dentro de la ceremonia del 25.º aniversario en el Monumento Conmemorativo del 11 de S.

segments.src: Twenty-five years to the day, the plaza at the National September 11 Memorial in Lower Manhattan filled once again with families holding photographs, folded flags, and small handwritten notes.
segments.tr: Veinticinco años exactos después, la plaza del Monumento Conmemorativo Nacional del 11 de Septiembre, en el Bajo Manhattan, se llenó una vez más de familias con fotografías, banderas dobladas y pequeñas notas escritas a mano.

segments.src: One by one, relatives stepped up to the microphones to read aloud the names of the 2,983 people killed in the attacks of September 11, 2001, and in the 1993 bombing of the World Trade Center.
segments.tr: Uno por uno, los familiares se acercaron a los micrófonos para leer en voz alta los nombres de las 2.983 personas fallecidas en los atentados del 11 de septiembre de 2001 y en el atentado de 1993 contra el World Trade Center.

segments.src: The reading, a tradition that has anchored the anniversary since the first year after the attacks, stretched across the morning as it has every year — but this quarter-century mark carried a weight of its own.
segments.tr: La lectura, una tradición que ha marcado el aniversario desde el primer año después de los atentados, se extendió a lo largo de la mañana como cada año, pero este cuarto de siglo cargaba con un peso propio.

segments.src: ## A Morning of Seven Silences
segments.tr: ## Una mañana de siete silencios

segments.src: The ceremony was structured, as always, around moments of silence that correspond to the timeline of that morning: the moment American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower, the moment United Airlines Flight 175 struck the South Tower, the moment American Airlines Flight 77 struck the Pentagon, the moment Flight 93 went down in a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, and the moments each tower fell.
segments.tr: La ceremonia se estructuró, como siempre, en torno a momentos de silencio que corresponden a la cronología de esa mañana: el momento en que el vuelo 11 de American Airlines impactó contra la Torre Norte, el momento en que el vuelo 175 de United Airlines impactó contra la Torre Sur, el momento en que el vuelo 77 de American Airlines impactó contra el Pentágono, el momento en que el vuelo 93 se estrelló en un campo cerca de Shanksville, Pensilvania, y los momentos en que cayó cada torre.

segments.src: Seven pauses in total, observed in near-total silence by the crowd gathered around the memorial's twin reflecting pools.
segments.tr: Siete pausas en total, guardadas en un silencio casi absoluto por la multitud reunida alrededor de las dos piscinas reflectantes del monumento conmemorativo.

segments.src: Bells tolled at the start of each pause.
segments.tr: Las campanas sonaron al comienzo de cada pausa.

segments.src: Many in attendance placed a hand over their heart; others simply stood still, eyes on the bronze parapets where the names of the dead are inscribed.
segments.tr: Muchos de los asistentes se colocaron una mano sobre el corazón; otros simplemente se quedaron quietos, con la mirada puesta en los parapetos de bronce donde están inscritos los nombres de los muertos.

segments.src: For families who have attended every anniversary since 2002, the rhythm of the ceremony is familiar.
segments.tr: Para las familias que han asistido a todos los aniversarios desde 2002, el ritmo de la ceremonia resulta familiar.

segments.src: For a younger generation attending for the first time — some too young to have been alive in 2001 — organizers say the ceremony has increasingly become a moment of historical connection as much as personal grief.
segments.tr: Para las generaciones más jóvenes que asisten por primera vez —algunas demasiado jóvenes para haber vivido en 2001—, los organizadores afirman que la ceremonia se ha convertido cada vez más en un momento de conexión histórica tanto como de duelo personal.

segments.src: ## Names Read by the Next Generation
segments.tr: ## Nombres leídos por la siguiente generación

segments.src: A notable feature of this year's reading was the number of children and grandchildren of victims taking the microphone, some reading a parent's or grandparent's name for the first time.
segments.tr: Un aspecto destacado de la lectura de este año fue la cantidad de hijos y nietos de las víctimas que tomaron el micrófono, algunos leyendo el nombre de un padre o abuelo por primera vez.

segments.src: Memorial organizers noted that as the population of surviving spouses and siblings ages, the responsibility of remembrance is passing to younger relatives — a shift that has shaped the tone of the ceremony in recent years toward continuity and legacy rather than only mourning.
segments.tr: Los organizadores del monumento señalaron que, a medida que envejece la población de cónyuges y hermanos sobrevivientes, la responsabilidad del recuerdo pasa a los familiares más jóvenes, un cambio que ha moldeado el tono de la ceremonia en los últimos años hacia la continuidad y el legado más que únicamente hacia el luto.

segments.src: Family members were also permitted, as in past years, to add brief personal remarks after reading each name — a line about a loved one's laugh, their profession, or a milestone the family has marked without them.
segments.tr: También se permitió a los familiares, como en años anteriores, añadir breves comentarios personales después de leer cada nombre: una frase sobre la risa de un ser querido, su profesión o un hito que la familia ha celebrado sin ellos.

segments.src: Memorial staff say these additions, while brief, have become one of the most meaningful parts of the day for attendees.
segments.tr: El personal del monumento afirma que estas adiciones, aunque breves, se han convertido en una de las partes más significativas del día para los asistentes.

segments.src: ## Tributes Beyond Manhattan
segments.tr: ## Homenajes más allá de Manhattan

segments.src: The commemorations extended well beyond the World Trade Center plaza.
segments.tr: Las conmemoraciones se extendieron mucho más allá de la plaza del World Trade Center.

segments.src: At the Pentagon Memorial in Arlington, Virginia, a separate ceremony honored the 184 people killed there, including those aboard Flight 77.
segments.tr: En el Monumento Conmemorativo del Pentágono en Arlington, Virginia, una ceremonia separada rindió homenaje a las 184 personas fallecidas allí, incluidos los ocupantes del vuelo 77.

segments.src: In Shanksville, Pennsylvania, the Flight 93 National Memorial held its own observance for the 40 passengers and crew who died after confronting hijackers, an act widely credited with preventing further attacks in Washington, D.C.
segments.tr: En Shanksville, Pensilvania, el Monumento Conmemorativo Nacional del Vuelo 93 celebró su propio acto en honor a los 40 pasajeros y tripulantes que murieron tras enfrentarse a los secuestradores, un acto al que se atribuye ampliamente haber evitado más ataques en Washington, D.C.

segments.src: Across New York City, firehouses, police precincts, and civic buildings held their own smaller tributes throughout the day, honoring the first responders — including the 343 firefighters and dozens of police officers — who died in the rescue efforts.
segments.tr: En toda la ciudad de Nueva York, los parques de bomberos, las comisarías de policía y los edificios cívicos celebraron sus propios homenajes más pequeños a lo largo del día, honrando a los servicios de emergencia —incluidos los 343 bomberos y decenas de policías— que murieron en las labores de rescate.

segments.src: Flags were lowered to half-staff at federal buildings nationwide, and moments of local remembrance were reported in communities across the country, reflecting how the events of that day touched nearly every state.
segments.tr: Las banderas ondearon a media asta en los edificios federales de todo el país, y se informaron momentos de recuerdo local en comunidades de todo el territorio nacional, lo que refleja cómo los acontecimientos de ese día afectaron a casi todos los estados.

segments.src: ## A Quarter-Century of Remembrance
segments.tr: ## Un cuarto de siglo de recuerdo

segments.src: Twenty-five years on, officials at the memorial say the annual reading remains one of the largest sustained acts of collective remembrance in the country.
segments.tr: Veinticinco años después, los responsables del monumento afirman sigue siendo uno de los mayores actos continuados de recuerdo colectivo del país.

segments.src: The names are read not in isolation but grouped where possible with family members' requests — husbands near wives, colleagues near colleagues — a practice memorial staff describe as an effort to preserve human connections in the record of the day.
segments.tr: Los nombres no se leen de forma aislada, sino agrupados siempre que es posible según las peticiones de los familiares —maridos cerca de esposas, compañeros cerca de compañeros—, una práctica que el personal del monumento describe como un esfuerzo por preservar las conexiones humanas en el registro de ese día.

segments.src: As the ceremony closed, attendees were invited to make paper rubbings of names etched into the memorial's bronze panels, a quiet ritual that has become part of the memorial's daily life beyond the anniversary itself.
segments.tr: Al clausurarse la ceremonia, se invitó a los asistentes a hacer calcas de papel de los nombres grabados en los paneles de bronce del monumento, un ritual silencioso que se ha convertido en parte de la vida diaria del monumento más allá del propio aniversario.

segments.src: For many families, the 25th anniversary was less about a milestone number than about ensuring the names — and the people behind them — continue to be spoken aloud, year after year.
segments.tr: Para muchas familias, el 25.º aniversario no consistió tanto en una cifra histórica como en garantizar que los nombres —y las personas que hay detrás de ellos— sigan siendo pronunciados en voz alta, año tras año.

segments.tr: واحداً تلو الآخر، صعد الأقارب إلى الميكروفونات لقراءة أسماء 2983 شخصاً قتلوا في هجمات 11 سبتمبر 2001، وفي تفجير مركز التجارة العالمي عام 1993.

segments.src: The reading, a tradition that has anchored the anniversary since the first year after the attacks, stretched across the morning as it has every year — but this quarter-century mark carried a weight of its own.
segments.tr: امتدت القراءة، وهي تقليد رسخ الذكرى السنوية منذ العام الأول بعد الهجمات، طوال الصباح كما يحدث كل عام - لكن علامة ربع القرن هذه حملت ثقلاً خاصاً بها.

segments.src: ## A Morning of Seven Silences
segments.tr: ## صباح من سبع لحظات صمت

segments.src: The ceremony was structured, as always, around moments of silence that correspond to the timeline of that morning: the moment American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower, the moment United Airlines Flight 175 struck the South Tower, the moment American Airlines Flight 77 struck the Pentagon, the moment Flight 93 went down in a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, and the moments each tower fell.
segments.tr: تم تنظيم المراسم، كما هو الحال دائماً، حول لحظات صمت تتوافق مع الجدول الزمني لذلك الصباح: اللحظة التي اصطدمت فيها رحلة الخطوط الجوية الأمريكية رقم 11 بالبرج الشمالي، واللحظة التي اصطدمت فيها رحلة الخطوط الجوية المتحدة رقم 175 بالبرج الجنوبي، واللحظة التي اصطدمت فيها رحلة الخطوط الجوية الأمريكية رقم 77 بالبنتاغون، واللحظة التي سقطت فيها الرحلة 93 في حقل بالقرب من شانكسفيل بولاية بنسلفانيا، ولحظات سقوط كل برج.

segments.src: Seven pauses in total, observed in near-total silence by the crowd gathered around the memorial's twin reflecting pools.
segments.tr: سبع وقفات في المجموع، تم رصدها في صمت شبه تام من قبل الحشد المتجمع حول بركتي النصب التذكاري العاكسة.

segments.src: Bells tolled at the start of each pause.
segments.tr: دقت الأجراس في بداية كل وقفة.

segments.src: Many in attendance placed a hand over their heart; others simply stood still, eyes on the bronze parapets where the names of the dead are inscribed.
segments.tr: وضع الكثير من الحاضرين أيديهم على قلوبهم؛ بينما وقف آخرون ببساطة دون حراك، وعيونهم على الحواجز البرونزية حيث نُقشت أسماء الموتى.

segments.src: For families who have attended every anniversary since 2002, the rhythm of the ceremony is familiar.
segments.tr: بالنسبة للعائلات التي حضرت كل ذكرى سنوية منذ عام 2002، فإن إيقاع المراسم مألوف.

segments.src: For a younger generation attending for the first time — some too young to have been alive in 2001 — organizers say the ceremony has increasingly become a moment of historical connection as much as personal grief.
segments.tr: بالنسبة لجيل أصغر يحضر للمرة الأولى - وبعضهم كان صغيراً جداً لدرجة أنهم لم يولدوا في عام 2001 - يقول المنظمون إن المراسم أصبحت بشكل متزايد لحظة تواصل تاريخي بقدر ما هي حزن شخصي.

segments.src: ## Names Read by the Next Generation
segments.tr: ## أسماء يقرؤها الجيل القادم

segments.src: A notable feature of this year's reading was the number of children and grandchildren of victims taking the microphone, some reading a parent's or grandparent's name for the first time.
segments.tr: كانت إحدى السمات البارزة لقراءة هذا العام هي عدد الأطفال والأحفاد للضحايا الذين اعتلو المنصة، حيث قرأ بعضهم اسم أحد الوالدين أو الأجداد للمرة الأولى.

segments.src: Memorial organizers noted that as the population of surviving spouses and siblings ages, the responsibility of remembrance is passing to younger relatives — a shift that has shaped the tone of the ceremony in recent years toward continuity and legacy rather than only mourning.
segments.tr: أشار منظمو النصب التذكاري إلى أنه مع تقدم عمر الأزواج والأشقاء الناجين، تنتقل مسؤولية الإحياء إلى الأقارب الأصغر سناً - وهو تحول شكل نبرة المراسم في السنوات الأخيرة نحو الاستمرارية والإرث بدلاً من الحداد فقط.

segments.src: Family members were also permitted, as in past years, to add brief personal remarks after reading each name — a line about a loved one's laugh, their profession, or a milestone the family has marked without them.
segments.tr: سُمح لأفراد العائلات أيضاً، كما في السنوات الماضية، بإضافة ملاحظات شخصية موجزة بعد قراءة كل اسم - جملة عن ضحكة أحد الأحباء، أو مهنتهم، أو إنجاز احتفلت به العائلة بدونهم.

segments.src: Memorial staff say these additions, while brief, have become one of the most meaningful parts of the day for attendees.
segments.tr: يقول موظفو النصب التذكاري إن هذه الإضافات، رغم إيجازها، أصبحت واحدة من أكثر أجزاء اليوم مغزى للحاضرين.

segments.src: ## Tributes Beyond Manhattan
segments.tr: ## تكريمات خارج مانهاتن

segments.src: The commemorations extended well beyond the World Trade Center plaza.
segments.tr: امتدت الاحتفالات إلى ما هو أبعد من ساحة مركز التجارة العالمي.

segments.src: At the Pentagon Memorial in Arlington, Virginia, a separate ceremony honored the 184 people killed there, including those aboard Flight 77.
segments.tr: في نصب البنتاغون التذكاري في أرلينغتون بولاية فيرجينيا، كرمت مراسم منفصلة الأشخاص الـ 184 الذين قتلوا هناك، بمن فيهم أولئك الذين كانوا على متن الرحلة 77.

segments.src: In Shanksville, Pennsylvania, the Flight 93 National Memorial held its own observance for the 40 passengers and crew who died after confronting hijackers, an act widely credited with preventing further attacks in Washington, D.C.
segments.tr: في شانكسفيل بولاية بنسلفانيا، أقام النصب التذكاري الوطني للرحلة 93 مراسم خاصة للركاب وأفراد الطاقم الأربعين الذين لقوا حتفهم بعد مواجهة الخاطفين، وهو عمل يُنسب إليه الفضل على نطاق واسع في منع وقوع هجمات أخرى في واشنطن العاصمة.

segments.src: Across New York City, firehouses, police precincts, and civic buildings held their own smaller tributes throughout the day, honoring the first responders — including the 343 firefighters and dozens of police officers — who died in the rescue efforts.
segments.tr: في جميع أنحاء مدينة نيويورك، أقامت محطات الإطفاء، ومراكز الشرطة، والمباني المدنية تكريمات أصغر خاصة بها طوال اليوم، تكريماً للمستجيبين الأوائل - بما في ذلك 343 رجل إطفاء وعشرات من ضباط الشرطة - الذين لقوا حتفهم في جهود الإنقاذ.

segments.src: Flags were lowered to half-staff at federal buildings nationwide, and moments of local remembrance were reported in communities across the country, reflecting how the events of that day touched nearly every state.
segments.tr: تم تنكيس الأعلام إلى نصف السارية في المباني الفيدرالية في جميع أنحاء البلاد، وتم الإبلاغ عن لحظات إحياء ذكرى محلية في مجتمعات في جميع أنحاء البلاد، مما يعكس كيف أثرت أحداث ذلك اليوم على كل ولاية تقريباً.

segments.src: ## A Quarter-Century of Remembrance
segments.tr: ## ربع قرن من الإحياء

segments.src: Twenty-five years on, officials at the memorial say the annual reading remains one of the largest sustained acts of collective remembrance in the country.
segments.tr: بعد خمسة وعشرين عاماً، يقول المسؤولون في النصب التذكاري إن القراءة السنوية تظل واحدة من أكبر أعمال الإحياء الجماعي المستمرة في البلاد.

segments.src: The names are read not in isolation but grouped where possible with family members' requests — husbands near wives, colleagues near colleagues — a practice memorial staff describe as an effort to preserve human connections in the record of the day.
segments.tr: لا تُقرأ الأسماء بمعزل عن بعضها البعض، بل يتم تجميعها حيثما أمكن ذلك بناءً على طلبات أفراد العائلة - الأزواج بالقرب من زوجاتهم، والزملاء بالقرب من زملائهم - وهي ممارسة يصفها موظفو النصب التذكاري بأنها جهد للحفاظ على الروابط الإنسانية في سجل ذلك اليوم.

segments.src: As the ceremony closed, attendees were invited to make paper rubbings of names etched into the memorial's bronze panels, a quiet ritual that has become part of the memorial's daily life beyond the anniversary itself.
segments.tr: مع اختتام المراسم، دُعي الحاضرون لأخذ طبعات ورقية للأسماء المحفورة في الألواح البرونزية للنصب التذكاري، وهو طقس هادئ أصبح جزءاً من الحياة اليومية للنصب التذكاري بعيداً عن الذكرى السنوية نفسها.

segments.src: For many families, the 25th anniversary was less about a milestone number than about ensuring the names — and the people behind them — continue to be spoken aloud, year after year.
segments.tr: بالنسبة للعديد من العائلات، لم تكن الذكرى الخامسة والعشرون تتعلق برقم تاريخي بقدر ما تتعلق بضمان استمرار نطق الأسماء - والأشخاص الذين يقفون خلفها - بصوت عالٍ، عاماً بعد عام.

fr.title: 2 983 noms, sept silences : Au cœur de la cérémonie du 25e anniversaire au mémorial du 11 septembre

segments.src: Twenty-five years to the day, the plaza at the National September 11 Memorial in Lower Manhattan filled once again with families holding photographs, folded flags, and small handwritten notes.
segments.tr: Vingt-cinq ans jour pour jour, l'esplanade du mémorial national du 11 septembre dans le Lower Manhattan s'est à nouveau remplie de familles tenant des photographies, des drapeaux pliés et de petits mots écrits à la main.

segments.src: One by one, relatives stepped up to the microphones to read aloud the names of the 2,983 people killed in the attacks of September 11, 2001, and in the 1993 bombing of the World Trade Center.
segments.tr: Un par un, les proches se sont approchés des micros pour lire à haute voix les noms des 2 983 personnes tuées lors des attentats du 11 septembre 2001 et de l'attentat à la bombe du World Trade Center en 1993.

segments.src: The reading, a tradition that has anchored the anniversary since the first year after the attacks, stretched across the morning as it has every year — but this quarter-century mark carried a weight of its own.
segments.tr: La lecture, une tradition qui ancre cet anniversaire depuis la première année suivant les attentats, s'est étirée tout au long de la matinée comme chaque année — mais ce quart de siècle d'existence portait un poids bien particulier.

segments.src: ## A Morning of Seven Silences
segments.tr: ## Une matinée de sept silences

segments.src: The ceremony was structured, as always, around moments of silence that correspond to the timeline of that morning: the moment American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower, the moment United Airlines Flight 175 struck the South Tower, the moment American Airlines Flight 77 struck the Pentagon, the moment Flight 93 went down in a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, and the moments each tower fell.
segments.tr: La cérémonie était structurée, comme toujours, autour de moments de silence correspondant à la chronologie de cette matinée-là : l'instant où le vol American Airlines 11 a percuté la tour Nord, l'instant où le vol United Airlines 175 a percuté la tour Sud, l'instant où le vol American Airlines 77 a percuté le Pentagone, l'instant où le vol 93 s'est écrasé dans un champ près de Shanksville, en Pennsylvanie, et les instants où chaque tour s'est effondrée.

segments.src: Seven pauses in total, observed in near-total silence by the crowd gathered around the memorial's twin reflecting pools.
segments.tr: Sept pauses au total, observées dans un silence quasi absolu par la foule rassemblée autour des deux bassins réfléchissants du mémorial.

segments.src: Bells tolled at the start of each pause.
segments.tr: Les cloches ont sonné au début de chaque pause.

segments.src: Many in attendance placed a hand over their heart; others simply stood still, eyes on the bronze parapets where the names of the dead are inscribed.
segments.tr: De nombreuses personnes présentes ont posé une main sur leur cœur ; d'autres sont simplement restées immobiles, les yeux fixés sur les parapets de bronze où sont gravés les noms des défunts.

segments.src: For families who have attended every anniversary since 2002, the rhythm of the ceremony is familiar.
segments.tr: Pour les familles qui ont assisté à chaque anniversaire depuis 2002, le rythme de la cérémonie est familier.

segments.src: For a younger generation attending for the first time — some too young to have been alive in 2001 — organizers say the ceremony has increasingly become a moment of historical connection as much as personal grief.
segments.tr: Pour une génération plus jeune qui y assiste pour la première fois — certains étant trop jeunes pour avoir été en vie en 2001 —, les organisateurs affirment que la cérémonie est de plus en plus devenue un moment de connexion historique autant que de deuil personnel.

segments.src: ## Names Read by the Next Generation
segments.tr: ## Des noms lus par la génération suivante

segments.src: A notable feature of this year's reading was the number of children and grandchildren of victims taking the microphone, some reading a parent's or grandparent's name for the first time.
segments.tr: Une caractéristique notable de la lecture de cette année a été le nombre d'enfants et de petits-enfants de victimes qui ont pris le micro, certains lisant le nom d'un parent ou d'un grand-parent pour la toute première fois.

segments.src: Memorial organizers noted that as the population of surviving spouses and siblings ages, the responsibility of remembrance is passing to younger relatives — a shift that has shaped the tone of the ceremony in recent years toward continuity and legacy rather than only mourning.
segments.tr: Les organisateurs du mémorial ont souligné qu'à mesure que la population des conjoints et frères et sœurs survivants vieillit, la responsabilité du souvenir se transmet aux plus jeunes proches — un changement qui a façonné le ton de la cérémonie ces dernières années vers la continuité et l'héritage plutôt que vers le seul deuil.

segments.src: Family members were also permitted, as in past years, to add brief personal remarks after reading each name — a line about a loved one's laugh, their profession, or a milestone the family has marked without them.
segments.tr: Les membres des familles étaient également autorisés, comme les années précédentes, à ajouter de brèves remarques personnelles après avoir lu chaque nom — un mot sur le rire d'un être cher, sa profession ou une étape importante que la famille a franchie sans lui.

segments.src: Memorial staff say these additions, while brief, have become one of the most meaningful parts of the day for attendees.
segments.tr: Le personnel du mémorial affirme que ces ajouts, bien que brefs, sont devenus l'un des moments les plus significatifs de la journée pour les participants.

segments.src: ## Tributes Beyond Manhattan
segments.tr: ## Des hommages au-delà de Manhattan

segments.src: The commemorations extended well beyond the World Trade Center plaza.
segments.tr: Les commémorations se sont étendues bien au-delà de l'esplanade du World Trade Center.

segments.src: At the Pentagon Memorial in Arlington, Virginia, a separate ceremony honored the 184 people killed there, including those aboard Flight 77.
segments.tr: Au mémorial du Pentagone à Arlington, en Virginie, une cérémonie distincte a rendu hommage aux 184 personnes qui y ont été tuées, y compris celles à bord du vol 77.

segments.src: In Shanksville, Pennsylvania, the Flight 93 National Memorial held its own observance for the 40 passengers and crew who died after confronting hijackers, an act widely credited with preventing further attacks in Washington, D.C.
segments.tr: À Shanksville, en Pennsylvanie, le mémorial national du vol 93 a organisé sa propre cérémonie pour les 40 passagers et membres d'équipage décédés après avoir affronté les pirates de l'air, un acte largement reconnu pour avoir empêché d'autres attaques à Washington, D.C.

segments.src: Across New York City, firehouses, police precincts, and civic buildings held their own smaller tributes throughout the day, honoring the first responders — including the 343 firefighters and dozens of police officers — who died in the rescue efforts.
segments.tr: Dans tout New York, les casernes de pompiers, les commissariats de police et les bâtiments civils ont organisé leurs propres hommages plus modestes tout au long de la journée, honorant les premiers intervenants — dont les 343 pompiers et des dizaines de policiers — morts dans les efforts de sauvetage.

segments.src: Flags were lowered to half-staff at federal buildings nationwide, and moments of local remembrance were reported in communities across the country, reflecting how the events of that day touched nearly every state.
segments.tr: Les drapeaux ont été mis en berne sur les bâtiments fédéraux dans tout le pays, et des moments de recueillement local ont été signalés dans des communautés de tout le pays, reflétant la manière dont les événements de cette journée ont touché presque chaque État.

segments.src: ## A Quarter-Century of Remembrance
segments.tr: ## Un quart de siècle de souvenir

segments.src: Twenty-five years on, officials at the memorial say the annual reading remains one of the largest sustained acts of collective remembrance in the country.
segments.tr: Vingt-cinq ans plus tard, les responsables du mémorial affirment que la lecture annuelle reste l'un des plus grands actes continus de mémoire collective du pays.

segments.src: The names are read not in isolation but grouped where possible with family members' requests — husbands near wives, colleagues near colleagues — a practice memorial staff describe as an effort to preserve human connections in the record of the day.
segments.tr: Les noms ne sont pas lus de manière isolée, mais regroupés dans la mesure du possible selon les demandes des familles — les maris près des épouses, les collègues près des collègues —, une pratique que le personnel du mémorial décrit comme un effort pour préserver les liens humains dans le récit de cette journée.

segments.src: As the ceremony closed, attendees were invited to make paper rubbings of names etched into the memorial's bronze panels, a quiet ritual that has become part of the memorial's daily life beyond the anniversary itself.
segments.tr: À la clôture de la cérémonie, les participants ont été invités à réaliser des empreintes sur papier des noms gravés sur les plaques de bronze du mémorial, un rituel silencieux qui fait désormais partie de la vie quotidienne du mémorial au-delà de l'anniversaire lui-même.

segments.src: For many families, the 25th anniversary was less about a milestone number than about ensuring the names — and the people behind them — continue to be spoken aloud, year after year.
segments.tr: Pour de nombreuses familles, ce 25e anniversaire représentait moins un chiffre symbolique qu'une manière de s'assurer que les noms — et les personnes derrière eux — continuent d'être prononcés à haute voix, année après année.

pt.title: 2.983 Nomes, Sete Silêncios: Por Dentro da Cerimônia de 25º Aniversário no Memorial do 11 de Setembro

segments.src: Twenty-five years to the day, the plaza at the National September 11 Memorial in Lower Manhattan filled once again with families holding photographs, folded flags, and small handwritten notes.
segments.tr: Vinte e cinco anos depois, no mesmo dia, a praça do Memorial Nacional do 11 de Setembro, no Baixo Manhattan, encheu-se mais uma vez com famílias segurando fotografias, bandeiras dobradas e pequenos bilhetes escritos à mão.

segments.src: One by one, relatives stepped up to the microphones to read aloud the names of the 2,983 people killed in the attacks of September 11, 2001, and in the 1993 bombing of the World Trade Center.
segments.tr: Um por um, os parentes subiram aos microfones para ler em voz alta os nomes das 2.983 pessoas mortas nos ataques de 11 de setembro de 2001 e no atentado de 1993 ao World Trade Center.

segments.src: The reading, a tradition that has anchored the anniversary since the first year after the attacks, stretched across the morning as it has every year — but this quarter-century mark carried a weight of its own.
segments.tr: A leitura, uma tradição que ancorou o aniversário desde o primeiro ano após os ataques, estendeu-se pela manhã como tem acontecido todos os anos — mas este marco de um quarto de século carregava um peso próprio.

segments.src: ## A Morning of Seven Silences
segments.tr: ## Uma Manhã de Sete Silêncios

segments.src: The ceremony was structured, as always, around moments of silence that correspond to the timeline of that morning: the moment American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower, the moment United Airlines Flight 175 struck the South Tower, the moment American Airlines Flight 77 struck the Pentagon, the moment Flight 93 went down in a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, and the moments each tower fell.
segments.tr: A cerimônia foi estruturada, como sempre, em torno de momentos de silêncio que correspondem à cronologia daquela manhã: o momento em que o voo 11 da American Airlines atingiu a Torre Norte, o momento em que o voo 175 da United Airlines atingiu a Torre Sul, o momento em que o voo 77 da American Airlines atingiu o Pentágono, o momento em que o voo 93 caiu em um campo perto de Shanksville, Pensilvânia, e os momentos em que cada torre caiu.

segments.src: Seven pauses in total, observed in near-total silence by the crowd gathered around the memorial's twin reflecting pools.
segments.tr: Sete pausas no total, observadas em silêncio quase absoluto pela multidão reunida ao redor das duas piscinas espelhadas do memorial.

segments.src: Bells tolled at the start of each pause.
segments.tr: Sinos tocaram no início de cada pausa.

segments.src: Many in attendance placed a hand over their heart; others simply stood still, eyes on the bronze parapets where the names of the dead are inscribed.
segments.tr: Muitos dos presentes colocaram a mão sobre o coração; outros simplesmente ficaram parados, com os olhos fixos nos parapeitos de bronze onde os nomes dos mortos estão inscritos.

segments.src: For families who have attended every anniversary since 2002, the rhythm of the ceremony is familiar.
segments.tr: Para as famílias que compareceram a todos os aniversários desde 2002, o ritmo da cerimônia é familiar.

segments.src: For a younger generation attending for the first time — some too young to have been alive in 2001 — organizers say the ceremony has increasingly become a moment of historical connection as much as personal grief.
segments.tr: Para uma geração mais jovem que comparece pela primeira vez — alguns jovens demais para estarem vivos em 2001 — os organizadores dizem que a cerimônia tornou-se cada vez mais um momento de conexão histórica tanto quanto de luto pessoal.

segments.src: ## Names Read by the Next Generation
segments.tr: ## Nomes Lidos pela Próxima Geração

segments.src: A notable feature of this year's reading was the number of children and grandchildren of victims taking the microphone, some reading a parent's or grandparent's name for the first time.
segments.tr: Uma característica notável da leitura deste ano foi o número de filhos e netos de vítimas que assumiram o microfone, alguns lendo o nome de um pai ou avô pela primeira vez.

segments.src: Memorial organizers noted that as the population of surviving spouses and siblings ages, the responsibility of remembrance is passing to younger relatives — a shift that has shaped the tone of the ceremony in recent years toward continuity and legacy rather than only mourning.
segments.tr: Os organizadores do memorial observaram que, à medida que a população de cônjuges e irmãos sobreviventes envelhece, a responsabilidade da lembrança está passando para parentes mais jovens — uma mudança que moldou o tom da cerimônia nos últimos anos em direção à continuidade e ao legado, em vez de apenas ao luto.

segments.src: Family members were also permitted, as in past years, to add brief personal remarks after reading each name — a line about a loved one's laugh, their profession, or a milestone the family has marked without them.
segments.tr: Os familiares também tiveram permissão, como nos anos anteriores, para adicionar breves comentários pessoais após a leitura de cada nome — uma frase sobre o riso de um ente querido, sua profissão ou um marco que a família celebrou sem eles.

segments.src: Memorial staff say these additions, while brief, have become one of the most meaningful parts of the day for attendees.
segments.tr: A equipe do memorial diz que essas adições, embora breves, tornaram-se uma das partes mais significativas do dia para os participantes.

segments.src: ## Tributes Beyond Manhattan
segments.tr: ## Homenagens Além de Manhattan

segments.tr: Em Shanksville, Pensilvânia, o Memorial Nacional do Voo 93 realizou sua própria cerimônia para os 40 passageiros e tripulantes que morreram após confrontarem os sequestradores, um ato amplamente creditado por evitar mais ataques em Washington, D.C.

segments.src: Across New York City, firehouses, police precincts, and civic buildings held their own smaller tributes throughout the day, honoring the first responders — including the 343 firefighters and dozens of police officers — who died in the rescue efforts.
segments.tr: Por toda a cidade de Nova York, quartéis de bombeiros, delegacias de polícia e edifícios cívicos realizaram suas próprias homenagens menores ao longo do dia, honrando os socorristas — incluindo os 343 bombeiros e dezenas de policiais — que morreram nos esforços de resgate.

segments.src: Flags were lowered to half-staff at federal buildings nationwide, and moments of local remembrance were reported in communities across the country, reflecting how the events of that day touched nearly every state.
segments.tr: As bandeiras foram hasteadas a meio mastro em edifícios federais em todo o país, e momentos de lembrança local foram relatados em comunidades por todo o país, refletindo como os eventos daquele dia tocaram quase todos os estados.

segments.src: ## A Quarter-Century of Remembrance
segments.tr: ## Um Quarto de Século de Lembrança

segments.src: Twenty-five years on, officials at the memorial say the annual reading remains one of the largest sustained acts of collective remembrance in the country.
segments.tr: Vinte e cinco anos depois, as autoridades do memorial dizem que a leitura anual continua sendo um dos maiores atos sustentados de lembrança coletiva no país.

segments.src: The names are read not in isolation but grouped where possible with family members' requests — husbands near wives, colleagues near colleagues — a practice memorial staff describe as an effort to preserve human connections in the record of the day.
segments.tr: Os nomes não são lidos isoladamente, mas agrupados sempre que possível com os pedidos dos familiares — maridos perto de esposas, colegas perto de colegas — uma prática que a equipe do memorial descreve como um esforço para preservar as conexões humanas no registro do dia.

segments.src: As the ceremony closed, attendees were invited to make paper rubbings of names etched into the memorial's bronze panels, a quiet ritual that has become part of the memorial's daily life beyond the anniversary itself.
segments.tr: Ao final da cerimônia, os participantes foram convidados a fazer decalques em papel dos nomes gravados nos painéis de bronze do memorial, um ritual silencioso que se tornou parte da vida diária do memorial além do próprio aniversário.

segments.src: For many families, the 25th anniversary was less about a milestone number than about ensuring the names — and the people behind them — continue to be spoken aloud, year after year.
segments.tr: Para muitas famílias, o 25º aniversário foi menos sobre um número marcante do que sobre garantir que os nomes — e as pessoas por trás deles — continuem a ser ditos em voz alta, ano após ano.

in.title: 2.983 Nama, Tujuh Keheningan: Di Dalam Upacara Peringatan 25 Tahun di Peringatan 9/11

segments.src: Twenty-five years to the day, the plaza at the National September 11 Memorial in Lower Manhattan filled once again with families holding photographs, folded flags, and small handwritten notes.
segments.tr: Dua puluh lima tahun pasca hari tersebut, alun-alun di National September 11 Memorial di Lower Manhattan kembali dipenuhi oleh keluarga-keluarga yang memegang foto, bendera yang dilipat, dan catatan kecil tulisan tangan.

segments.src: One by one, relatives stepped up to the microphones to read aloud the names of the 2,983 people killed in the attacks of September 11, 2001, and in the 1993 bombing of the World Trade Center.
segments.tr: Satu per satu, para kerabat maju ke mikrofon untuk membacakan nama-nama dari 2.983 orang yang tewas dalam serangan 11 September 2001, dan dalam pengeboman World Trade Center tahun 1993.

segments.src: The reading, a tradition that has anchored the anniversary since the first year after the attacks, stretched across the morning as it has every year — but this quarter-century mark carried a weight of its own.
segments.tr: Pembacaan tersebut, sebuah tradisi yang telah menjadi jangkar peringatan sejak tahun pertama setelah serangan, berlangsung sepanjang pagi seperti tahun-tahun sebelumnya — namun peringatan seperempat abad ini membawa bebannya tersendiri.

segments.src: ## A Morning of Seven Silences
segments.tr: ## Pagi dengan Tujuh Keheningan

segments.src: The ceremony was structured, as always, around moments of silence that correspond to the timeline of that morning: the moment American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower, the moment United Airlines Flight 175 struck the South Tower, the moment American Airlines Flight 77 struck the Pentagon, the moment Flight 93 went down in a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, and the moments each tower fell.
segments.tr: Upacara ini disusun, seperti biasa, di sekitar momen-momen keheningan yang sesuai dengan linimasa pagi itu: saat penerbangan American Airlines Flight 11 menabrak Menara Utara, saat penerbangan United Airlines Flight 175 menabrak Menara Selatan, saat penerbangan American Airlines Flight 77 menabrak Pentagon, saat Flight 93 jatuh di sebuah lapangan dekat Shanksville, Pennsylvania, dan saat masing-masing menara runtuh.

segments.src: Seven pauses in total, observed in near-total silence by the crowd gathered around the memorial's twin reflecting pools.
segments.tr: Tujuh jeda secara total, diamati dalam keheningan hampir total oleh kerumunan yang berkumpul di sekitar dua kolam refleksi tugu peringatan.

segments.src: Bells tolled at the start of each pause.
segments.tr: Lonceng berdentang pada awal setiap jeda.

segments.src: Many in attendance placed a hand over their heart; others simply stood still, eyes on the bronze parapets where the names of the dead are inscribed.
segments.tr: Banyak yang hadir meletakkan tangan di dada mereka; yang lain hanya berdiri diam, mata tertuju pada pembatas perunggu tempat nama-nama korban tewas diukir.

segments.src: For families who have attended every anniversary since 2002, the rhythm of the ceremony is familiar.
segments.tr: Bagi keluarga yang telah menghadiri setiap peringatan sejak tahun 2002, ritme upacara tersebut sudah tidak asing lagi.

segments.src: For a younger generation attending for the first time — some too young to have been alive in 2001 — organizers say the ceremony has increasingly become a moment of historical connection as much as personal grief.
segments.tr: Bagi generasi muda yang hadir untuk pertama kalinya — beberapa terlalu muda untuk hidup pada tahun 2001 — penyelenggara mengatakan upacara tersebut semakin menjadi momen hubungan historis sekaligus kesedihan pribadi.

segments.src: ## Names Read by the Next Generation
segments.tr: ## Nama-Nama yang Dibacakan oleh Generasi Berikutnya

segments.src: A notable feature of this year's reading was the number of children and grandchildren of victims taking the microphone, some reading a parent's or grandparent's name for the first time.
segments.tr: Fitur penting dari pembacaan tahun ini adalah jumlah anak-anak dan cucu-cucu korban yang naik ke mikrofon, beberapa membaca nama orang tua atau kakek-nenek untuk pertama kalinya.

segments.src: Memorial organizers noted that as the population of surviving spouses and siblings ages, the responsibility of remembrance is passing to younger relatives — a shift that has shaped the tone of the ceremony in recent years toward continuity and legacy rather than only mourning.
segments.tr: Penyelenggara tugu peringatan mencatat bahwa seiring bertambahnya usia populasi pasangan dan saudara kandung yang selamat, tanggung jawab mengenang beralih ke kerabat yang lebih muda — sebuah pergeseran yang telah membentuk nada upacara dalam beberapa tahun terakhir menuju kesinambungan dan warisan alih-alih hanya berduka.

segments.src: Family members were also permitted, as in past years, to add brief personal remarks after reading each name — a line about a loved one's laugh, their profession, or a milestone the family has marked without them.
segments.tr: Anggota keluarga juga diizinkan, seperti tahun-tahun sebelumnya, untuk menambahkan ucapan pribadi singkat setelah membaca setiap nama — sepenggal kalimat tentang tawa orang tercinta, profesi mereka, atau pencapaian yang telah ditandai keluarga tanpa kehadiran mereka.

segments.src: Memorial staff say these additions, while brief, have become one of the most meaningful parts of the day for attendees.
segments.tr: Staf tugu peringatan mengatakan penambahan ini, meskipun singkat, telah menjadi salah satu bagian paling bermakna dari hari tersebut bagi para peserta.

segments.src: ## Tributes Beyond Manhattan
segments.tr: ## Penghormatan di Luar Manhattan

segments.src: The commemorations extended well beyond the World Trade Center plaza.
segments.tr: Peringatan tersebut meluas jauh melampaui alun-alun World Trade Center.

segments.src: At the Pentagon Memorial in Arlington, Virginia, a separate ceremony honored the 184 people killed there, including those aboard Flight 77.
segments.tr: Di Pentagon Memorial di Arlington, Virginia, sebuah upacara terpisah menghormati 184 orang yang tewas di sana, termasuk mereka yang berada di dalam Flight 77.

segments.src: In Shanksville, Pennsylvania, the Flight 93 National Memorial held its own observance for the 40 passengers and crew who died after confronting hijackers, an act widely credited with preventing further attacks in Washington, D.C.
segments.tr: Di Shanksville, Pennsylvania, Flight 93 National Memorial mengadakan peringatannya sendiri untuk 40 penumpang dan kru yang tewas setelah menghadapi para pembajak, sebuah tindakan yang secara luas dianggap mencegah serangan lebih lanjut di Washington, D.C.

segments.src: Across New York City, firehouses, police precincts, and civic buildings held their own smaller tributes throughout the day, honoring the first responders — including the 343 firefighters and dozens of police officers — who died in the rescue efforts.
segments.tr: Di seluruh Kota New York, markas pemadam kebakaran, kantor polisi, dan bangunan sipil mengadakan penghormatan yang lebih kecil sepanjang hari, menghormati para petugas tanggap darurat — termasuk 343 petugas pemadam kebakaran dan puluhan petugas polisi — yang tewas dalam upaya penyelamatan.

segments.src: Flags were lowered to half-staff at federal buildings nationwide, and moments of local remembrance were reported in communities across the country, reflecting how the events of that day touched nearly every state.
segments.tr: Bendera diturunkan setengah tiang di gedung-gedung federal secara nasional, dan momen-momen peringatan lokal dilaporkan di berbagai komunitas di seluruh negeri, mencerminkan bagaimana peristiwa hari itu menyentuh hampir setiap negara bagian.

segments.src: ## A Quarter-Century of Remembrance
segments.tr: ## Seperempat Abad Mengenang

segments.src: Twenty-five years on, officials at the memorial say the annual reading remains one of the largest sustained acts of collective remembrance in the country.
segments.tr: Dua puluh lima tahun berlalu, para pejabat di tugu peringatan mengatakan pembacaan tahunan tetap menjadi salah satu tindakan peringatan kolektif terbesar yang berkelanjutan di negara ini.

segments.src: The names are read not in isolation but grouped where possible with family members' requests — husbands near wives, colleagues near colleagues — a practice memorial staff describe as an effort to preserve human connections in the record of the day.
segments.tr: Nama-nama tersebut dibacakan bukan secara terisolasi melainkan dikelompokkan jika memungkinkan dengan permintaan anggota keluarga — suami di dekat istri, rekan kerja di dekat rekan kerja — sebuah praktik yang digambarkan oleh staf tugu peringatan sebagai upaya untuk melestarikan hubungan manusia dalam catatan hari itu.

segments.src: As the ceremony closed, attendees were invited to make paper rubbings of names etched into the memorial's bronze panels, a quiet ritual that has become part of the memorial's daily life beyond the anniversary itself.
segments.tr: Saat upacara ditutup, para peserta diundang untuk membuat gesekan kertas dari nama-nama yang terukir di panel perunggu tugu peringatan, sebuah ritual tenang yang telah menjadi bagian dari kehidupan sehari-hari tugu peringatan di luar peringatan itu sendiri.

segments.src: For many families, the 25th anniversary was less about a milestone number than about ensuring the names — and the people behind them — continue to be spoken aloud, year after year.
segments.tr: Bagi banyak keluarga, peringatan 25 tahun lebih berkaitan dengan memastikan nama-nama — dan orang-orang di balik nama tersebut — terus diucapkan dengan lantang, tahun demi tahun.

ja.title: 2,983人の名前、7回の黙祷：9.11メモリアル25周年記念式典の舞台裏

segments.src: Twenty-five years to the day, the plaza at the National September 11 Memorial in Lower Manhattan filled once again with families holding photographs, folded flags, and small handwritten notes.
segments.tr: あの日から25年、マンハッタン南部の9.11国立メモリアル広場は、再び写真や折りたたまれた旗、手書きの小さなメモを手にした家族たちで埋め尽くされました。

segments.src: One by one, relatives stepped up to the microphones to read aloud the names of the 2,983 people killed in the attacks of September 11, 2001, and in the 1993 bombing of the World Trade Center.
segments.tr: 遺族たちは一人ずつマイクの前に立ち、2001年9月11日の同時多発テロ、および1993年の世界貿易センター爆破事件で亡くなった2,983人の名前を読み上げました。

segments.src: The reading, a tradition that has anchored the anniversary since the first year after the attacks, stretched across the morning as it has every year — but this quarter-century mark carried a weight of its own.
segments.tr: テロ発生の翌年から毎年恒例となっているこの名前の読み上げは、例年通り午前中いっぱい続きましたが、四半世紀という節目には特別な重みがありました。

segments.src: ## A Morning of Seven Silences
segments.tr: ## 7回の黙祷が捧げられた朝

segments.src: The ceremony was structured, as always, around moments of silence that correspond to the timeline of that morning: the moment American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower, the moment United Airlines Flight 175 struck the South Tower, the moment American Airlines Flight 77 struck the Pentagon, the moment Flight 93 went down in a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, and the moments each tower fell.
segments.tr: 式典はこれまでと同様、あの日起きた出来事のタイムラインに合わせた黙祷を中心に構成されました。アメリカン航空11便が北棟に衝突した瞬間、ユナイテッド航空175便が南棟に衝突した瞬間、アメリカン航空77便がペンタゴンに衝突した瞬間、93便がペンシルベニア州シャンクスビル近郊の野原に墜落した瞬間、そしてそれぞれのタワーが崩壊した瞬間です。

segments.src: Seven pauses in total, observed in near-total silence by the crowd gathered around the memorial's twin reflecting pools.
segments.tr: 合計7回の黙祷が捧げられ、メモリアルの2つのリフレクティング・プール（追悼の池）の周りに集まった人々は、ほぼ完全な静寂の中で祈りを捧げました。

segments.src: Bells tolled at the start of each pause.
segments.tr: それぞれの黙祷の始まりには鐘が鳴らされました。

segments.src: Many in attendance placed a hand over their heart; others simply stood still, eyes on the bronze parapets where the names of the dead are inscribed.
segments.tr: 参列者の多くは胸に手を当て、またある者はただ静かに立ち、犠牲者の名前が刻まれたブロンズ製の欄干に目を向けていました。

segments.src: For families who have attended every anniversary since 2002, the rhythm of the ceremony is familiar.
segments.tr: 2002年以来、毎年欠かさず参列してきた家族にとって、式典の流れは馴染み深いものです。

segments.src: For a younger generation attending for the first time — some too young to have been alive in 2001 — organizers say the ceremony has increasingly become a moment of historical connection as much as personal grief.
segments.tr: 初めて参列する若い世代（中には2001年にはまだ生まれていなかった人もいます）にとって、この式典は個人的な悲しみの場であると同時に、歴史とのつながりを感じる場にもなりつつあると主催者は語ります。

segments.src: ## Names Read by the Next Generation
segments.tr: ## 次世代によって読み上げられる名前

segments.src: A notable feature of this year's reading was the number of children and grandchildren of victims taking the microphone, some reading a parent's or grandparent's name for the first time.
segments.tr: 今年の読み上げで特筆すべきは、犠牲者の子供や孫がマイクを握る姿が多く見られたことです。中には、親や祖父母の名前を初めて読み上げる人もいました。

segments.src: Memorial organizers noted that as the population of surviving spouses and siblings ages, the responsibility of remembrance is passing to younger relatives — a shift that has shaped the tone of the ceremony in recent years toward continuity and legacy rather than only mourning.
segments.tr: メモリアルの主催者は、生存している配偶者や兄弟姉妹が高齢化するにつれ、追悼の責任が若い親族へと引き継がれていると指摘しています。この変化により、近年、式典のトーンは単なる追悼から、継続と継承へとシフトしています。

segments.src: Family members were also permitted, as in past years, to add brief personal remarks after reading each name — a line about a loved one's laugh, their profession, or a milestone the family has marked without them.
segments.tr: 例年通り、家族は名前を読み上げた後に短い個人的なメッセージを添えることが許されました。愛する人の笑い声や職業、あるいは彼らがいなくなってから家族が迎えた節目についての言葉などが語られました。

segments.src: Memorial staff say these additions, while brief, have become one of the most meaningful parts of the day for attendees.
segments.tr: メモリアルのスタッフによると、こうした短い言葉こそが、参列者にとってこの日最も意味のある瞬間の一つになっているといいます。

segments.src: ## Tributes Beyond Manhattan
segments.tr: ## マンハッタン以外での追悼

segments.src: The commemorations extended well beyond the World Trade Center plaza.
segments.tr: 追悼行事は世界貿易センターの広場だけにとどまりませんでした。

segments.src: At the Pentagon Memorial in Arlington, Virginia, a separate ceremony honored the 184 people killed there, including those aboard Flight 77.
segments.tr: バージニア州アーリントンのペンタゴン・メモリアルでは、77便の搭乗者を含む184人の犠牲者を追悼する別の式典が行われました。

segments.src: In Shanksville, Pennsylvania, the Flight 93 National Memorial held its own observance for the 40 passengers and crew who died after confronting hijackers, an act widely credited with preventing further attacks in Washington, D.C.
segments.tr: ペンシルベニア州シャンクスビルのフライト93国立メモリアルでは、ハイジャック犯に立ち向かい、ワシントンD.C.でのさらなる攻撃を阻止したとされる40人の乗客と乗員を追悼する独自の式典が開催されました。

segments.src: Across New York City, firehouses, police precincts, and civic buildings held their own smaller tributes throughout the day, honoring the first responders — including the 343 firefighters and dozens of police officers — who died in the rescue efforts.
segments.tr: ニューヨーク市内の消防署、警察署、公共施設でも一日を通して小規模な追悼行事が行われ、救助活動中に亡くなった343人の消防士や数十人の警察官を含む、最初の対応者たち（ファーストレスポンダー）が称えられました。

segments.src: Flags were lowered to half-staff at federal buildings nationwide, and moments of local remembrance were reported in communities across the country, reflecting how the events of that day touched nearly every state.
segments.tr: 全米の連邦政府機関では半旗が掲げられ、各地のコミュニティでも追悼の瞬間が持たれました。これは、あの日起きた出来事が全米のほぼすべての州に影響を及ぼしたことを物語っています。

segments.src: ## A Quarter-Century of Remembrance
segments.tr: ## 四半世紀の追悼

segments.src: Twenty-five years on, officials at the memorial say the annual reading remains one of the largest sustained acts of collective remembrance in the country.
segments.tr: 25年が経過した今、メモリアルの関係者は、この毎年恒例の読み上げが、全米で最も大規模かつ継続的な集団追悼行事の一つであり続けていると語ります。

segments.src: The names are read not in isolation but grouped where possible with family members' requests — husbands near wives, colleagues near colleagues — a practice memorial staff describe as an effort to preserve human connections in the record of the day.
segments.tr: 名前は単独で読み上げられるのではなく、可能な限り家族の希望に沿ってグループ化されています（夫の近くに妻を、同僚の近くに同僚を）。これは、あの日を記録する上で人間同士のつながりを大切にしようとするメモリアルスタッフの取り組みです。

segments.src: As the ceremony closed, attendees were invited to make paper rubbings of names etched into the memorial's bronze panels, a quiet ritual that has become part of the memorial's daily life beyond the anniversary itself.
segments.tr: 式典の締めくくりには、参列者がメモリアルのブロンズパネルに刻まれた名前を紙に写し取る（拓本をとる）ことが推奨されました。これは、周年記念日以外でもメモリアルの日常の一部となっている静かな儀式です。

segments.src: For many families, the 25th anniversary was less about a milestone number than about ensuring the names — and the people behind them — continue to be spoken aloud, year after year.
segments.tr: 多くの家族にとって、25周年という節目は、数字そのものよりも、名前を、そしてその名前の背後にある人々を、年を追うごとに語り継いでいくことの重要性を再確認する機会となりました。
